questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “nn.Embedding” in this lesson?
options: This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.
Trace token IDs, sequence length, padding/causal masks, and prediction targets so the model only uses information available for the task.
This topic removes the need to validate inputs or inspect model outputs.
questions.answer_key: Trace token IDs, sequence length, padding/causal masks, and prediction targets so the model only uses information available for the task.
questions.explanation: nn.Embedding: Trace token IDs, sequence length, padding/causal masks, and prediction targets so the model only uses information available for the task.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Token embeddings”, what should a learner verify?
options: Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
verify token/target alignment, padding indices, attention masks, and causal masking where future tokens must be hidden.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
questions.answer_key: verify token/target alignment, padding indices, attention masks, and causal masking where future tokens must be hidden.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: verify token/target alignment, padding indices, attention masks, and causal masking where future tokens must be hidden.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Position embeddings”?
options: Do not let a language model attend to future target tokens during autoregressive training or evaluation.
Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
questions.answer_key: Do not let a language model attend to future target tokens during autoregressive training or evaluation.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not let a language model attend to future target tokens during autoregressive training or evaluation.
